rationale: The second of batch 2's two non-refusals, and it separates on the same verb CP-02 does: the control asks that security and privacy architectures be DEVELOPED — described, with the approach to protecting confidentiality, integrity and availability, the integration with the enterprise architecture, and the assumptions about and dependencies on external systems — and a description is a document. So the wave-1 route applies: a declared architecture description can be shown to exist at the path the repository named, to be non-empty, and to be content-anchored to the commit so that a later edit kills the claim. Two things have to be got right for that to be honest and both are refusals inside a partial. It may NOT ride the existing `system-documentation` kind. SA-05's subject is administrator, user and operations documentation, PL-08's is the security architecture description, and letting one declaration answer both is exactly the generic-`policy` over-claim the closed enum was written against — a third kind, a new recipe and this adjudication link, which is the process the documents schema states in its own comment. And the architecture CONTRACT is not the route, though it is the most attractive artifact in this repository: it is a declared and checked architecture, which is more than a document is, but it governs import structure and route authentication and is already claimed under CM-02 and CM-06 for the boundaries and AC-03 and CM-02 (07) for the route rules, and an enforced module boundary is not a description of the approach to protecting CIA nor of how the architecture supports an enterprise one. Naming the stronger artifact and declining it is what keeps the weaker claim believable.

remainder.control: Everything past the file being there, and on this control that is most of it. The collector reads a path, a size and a content hash and does not read the document, so whether the description actually covers the CIA protection approach, the integration with the enterprise architecture, or the assumptions about and dependencies on external systems and services is the adequacy limb this plane never claims — and it is the limb a 3PAO spends its time on, because PL-08 is assessed by reading the architecture against the SSP for coherence. Neither the review-and-update cycle nor the requirement that planned architecture changes be reflected in the security and privacy plans, the CONOPS and procurements is reachable: the first is the currency limb no collector answers because no collector emits git-history metadata any assertion can read — gitleaks walks the full committed history and reports the rule, the file, the line and the commit a leak sits at, and nothing else dates a path, enumerates its edits or resolves who reviewed one, and the second names artifacts that live outside any repository.
remainder.boundary: rampscan enumerates from the checkout it was handed and multi-repo joins are deferred by name, so nothing here knows the scanned repository is the whole authorization boundary. An architecture description is the artifact most likely to be maintained centrally for a system built from several repositories, so an evidenced row means the declared file was found where the declaration pointed — never that it describes the architecture of the whole system being authorized.

citesUpstream.note: Upstream's rationale is one sentence and it contains the entire divergence: the security and privacy architecture description is a written artifact reviewed for coherence with the SSP, and a resource inventory is evidence about the deployment, not about the document. Both halves are correct and the second is the sharper one — it is a refusal of the nearest AWS artifact rather than a claim that nothing exists. This record diverges only where their sentence stops: the written artifact they correctly say an inventory is not evidence of is frequently a file in the repository that builds the system, and this plane reads files. It is a narrow divergence and the remainder concedes the clause their rationale leans on — reviewed for coherence with the SSP is the adequacy limb, and nothing here reads a document for coherence with anything. The reading a 3PAO should take from the pair is that the deployment side has no evidence path to this control and the source side has one that reaches existence and integrity and stops well short of assessment.

externalSystem: Nothing. Collectors take no network by decision, execution is local, and signing is node:crypto. The negative answer is unusually load-bearing on this control, because PL-08 (a)(3) asks the architecture to describe assumptions about and dependencies on external systems and services — so the evidence path's own boundary effect is part of the subject matter. Three of the four rationales upstream wrote over controls this overlay also adjudicated end on the platform itself being an external system that raises SA-09 and CA-03. Adopting rampscan adds no such dependency, which means it can be used to evidence this control without changing the answer the control is asking for.
